'''Paul T. Anastas'''  (born May 16, 1962, in [[Quincy, Massachusetts]])<ref name="books-XOL6mgnGOHoC-185">David E. Newton: [https://books.google.com/books?id=XOL6mgnGOHoC&dq=%22Paul+Anastas%22+Quincy&pg=PA185 ''Chemistry of the Environment.''] Infobase Publishing, 2009, {{ISBN|978-1-438-10974-9}}, p.&nbsp;185.</ref> is an American scientist, inventor, author, entrepreneur, professor, and public servant. Paul Anastas is widely regarded as the "Father of Green Chemistry."<ref>[https://www.aaas.org/news/paul-anastas-father-green-chemistry-urges-new-cleaner-solutions-past-and-future-challenges Paul Anastas, the Father of Green Chemistry, Urges New, Cleaner Solutions for Past and Future Challenges]</ref><ref>[https://www.chemistryworld.com/culture/paul-anastas-im-proudest-of-being-part-of-a-global-green-chemistry-community/4020098.article Paul Anastas: 'I'm proudest of being part of a global green chemistry community']</ref><ref>[https://www.discovermagazine.com/scientist-you-should-know-paul-anastas-is-the-father-of-green-chemistry-43835 Scientist You Should Know: Paul Anastas is the Father of Green Chemistry]</ref> He is the Program Director of the Green Chemistry Initiative at the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation. In 2007 he co-founded the [[Yale University]]'s Center for [[Green chemistry|Green Chemistry]] and Green Engineering.<ref name="greenchemistry.yale.edu">{{Cite web|url=https://greenchemistry.yale.edu/|title=Center for Green Chemistry & Green Engineering at Yale &#124;|website=greenchemistry.yale.edu}}</ref>  Previously he served as the Science Advisor to the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.epa.gov/research|title=Research|first=ORD|last=US EPA|date=June 10, 2013|website=[[United States Environmental Protection Agency]]}}</ref> as well as the Agency's Assistant Administrator for [[Research and Development]], appointed by President [[Barack Obama]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brandeis.eduanastasnomination.html/|title=President Obama nominates Paul Anastas, MS'87, PhD'90, to EPA post|website=BrandeisNOW}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

== Career ==
Anastas is known widely for his work on the design and manufacture of chemicals that are non-hazardous and environmentally benign. He is also a champion of sustainability science and innovation for environmental protection.

Anastas has brought worldwide attention to the power of molecular design to help the environment.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Voutchkova |first1=Adelina M. |last2=Ferris |first2=Lori A. |last3=Zimmerman |first3=Julie B. |last4=Anastas |first4=Paul T. |title=Toward molecular design for hazard reduction—fundamental relationships between chemical properties and toxicity |journal=Tetrahedron |date=January 2010 |volume=66 |issue=5 |pages=1031–1039 |doi=10.1016/j.tet.2009.11.002 }}</ref> He has published scores of articles as well as fifteen books,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goodreads.com/author/list/235867.Paul_T_Anastas|title=Books by Paul T. Anastas (Author of Green Chemistry)|website=www.goodreads.com}}</ref> including his seminal work with co-author [[John Warner (chemist)|John Warner]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.warnerbabcock.com/about_wbi/john_warner.asp|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100129060802/http://www.warnerbabcock.com/about_wbi/john_warner.asp|url-status=dead|title=John Warner Bio|archivedate=January 29, 2010}}</ref> ''Green Chemistry: Theory and Practice''. Their [[Green chemistry#Principles|12 Principles of Green Chemistry]] are the basis for high school, college and graduate programs around the world<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://advancinggreenchemistry.org/cgi-sys/suspendedpage.cgi?page_id=686|title=Account Suspended|website=advancinggreenchemistry.org|date=10 March 2024 }}</ref> and have significantly altered the landscape of the chemicals industry in the United States and other countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.greenbiz.com/news/2010/03/16/greem-chemistry-becomes-core-element-industry|title=GreenBiz Article on Green Chemistry|access-date=2011-06-16|archive-date=2018-08-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180804053155/https://www.greenbiz.com/news/2010/03/16/greem-chemistry-becomes-core-element-industry|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Anastas began his career as a staff chemist at the EPA, where he coined the term "Green Chemistry"<ref name="yalescientific.org">{{Cite web|url=https://www.yalescientific.org/2010/10/paul-anastas-a-power-player-in-the-global-chemical-industry/|title=Paul Anastas: A Power Player in the Global Chemical Industry – Yale Scientific Magazine|website=www.yalescientific.org}}</ref> and launched the field's first research program. He went on to co-found the Green Chemistry Institute in 1997<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en.html|title=American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society}}</ref> at the [[American Chemical Society]] and served in the White House [[Office of Science and Technology Policy]] from 1999 to 2004, where he concluded service as Assistant Director for the Environment. Anastas returned to EPA in 2009 as the Assistant Administrator for EPA's Office of Research and Development (ORD) and the Science Advisor to the Agency, resigning from those positions in February 2012 to return to Yale and his family.  In his role as Assistant Administrator, he worked to engage scientists, engineers, and stakeholders across EPA, the [[Federal government of the United States|federal government]], and the [[scientific community]] to unify around the common goal of sustainability.<ref name = "mr. sustainability">{{Cite web|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/government/88/8817gov1.html|title=C&EN: Mr. Sustainability Goes to Washington}}</ref> He co-founded the chemical manufacturing company, P2 Science in 2011, the catalysis company, Catalytic Innovations in 2017, and Inkemia Green Chemicals in 2017. Anastas is currently on leave from Yale where he was the Director of [[Yale University]]'s Center for Green Chemistry and Green Engineering,<ref name="greenchemistry.yale.edu"/> where he holds the Theresa and H. John Heinz chair in Chemistry for the Environment.

== Early life ==
Anastas was born and raised in [[Quincy, Massachusetts]]. He developed an interest in science and environmental issues after witnessing the [[wetlands]] behind his childhood home get bulldozed and destroyed for a development project.<ref name = "guru">[https://www.nytimes.com/gwire/2011/06/20/20greenwire-green-chemistry-guru-charting-new-course-for-e-47583.html "Green Chemistry Guru Charting New Course at EPA"]. ''The New York Times''.</ref> When he was nine years old he received an “Award of Excellence” from President Richard Nixon for his “outstanding achievements in environmental protection” for his essay on the founding of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. As a teenager in Quincy, Anastas met and developed a close friendship with fellow green chemist John Warner. The pair have since co-authored several scientific papers and books, including the 12 Principles of Green Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.onearth.org/article/pure-chemistry|title=OnEarth: Pure Chemistry}}</ref> Anastas retains a noticeable [[Boston accent]] and is a devoted fan of his hometown baseball team, the [[Boston Red Sox]].<ref name = "guru"/>

He is trained as a [[synthetic organic chemistry|synthetic organic chemist]]. He earned his B.S. in chemistry from the [[University of Massachusetts#University of Massachusetts Boston|University of Massachusetts Boston]] and his M.A. and Ph.D. in chemistry from [[Brandeis University]].

== Public speaking ==
[[File:Paul Anastas speaking.jpg|thumb|Paul Anastas speaking on Earth Day. April, 2010]]Anastas is known for delivering energetic, engaging public talks that challenge audience members to think differently about environmental challenges.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.neiwpcc.org/email-newsletter/May2011/may2011.html|title=Thinking Differently|access-date=2011-06-25|archive-date=2012-03-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120326022931/http://www.neiwpcc.org/email-newsletter/May2011/may2011.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> His speeches have been called "thought provoking",<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.iprd.leeds.ac.uk/news.php|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120307160718/http://www.iprd.leeds.ac.uk/news.php|url-status=dead|title=University of Leeds: Industrial Club Talk|archivedate=March 7, 2012}}</ref> "inspiring",<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blog.epa.gov/blog/2010/10/20/science-wednesday-%E2%80%9Cnifty-fifty%E2%80%9D-scientist-inspires-next-generations-of-innovators/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008190452/http://blog.epa.gov/blog/2010/10/20/science-wednesday-%E2%80%9Cnifty-fifty%E2%80%9D-scientist-inspires-next-generations-of-innovators/|url-status=dead|title=EPA Blog: Nifty Fifty Talk|archivedate=October 8, 2011}}</ref> and "optimistic".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sustainable-living-blog.com/?p=6 |title=Sustainable Living Blog: ACS Green Chemistry Talk |access-date=2011-06-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100712071441/http://sustainable-living-blog.com/?p=6 |archive-date=2010-07-12 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has been featured as a [[keynote speaker]] at several prestigious meetings, conferences and events, including:

* The American College and University President's Climate Commitment Summit<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hotelnew-york.net/da/presidentsclimatecommitment.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120311114421/http://www2.presidentsclimatecommitment.org/2011-summit/attendees.html|url-status=dead|title=Home &#124; Presidents' Climate Commitment &#124; Insiderguiden til New York-hoteller|archivedate=March 11, 2012|website=www.hotelnew-york.net}}</ref>
* The [[Joseph Priestley]] Lecture at the [[Chemical Heritage Foundation]]
* The [[United Nations]] [[Commission on Sustainable Development]] Roundtable<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.un.org/News/Press/docs/2011/envdev1211.doc.htm|title=UN Roundtable}}</ref>
* The [[Albemarle Corporation|Albemarle]] Lecture on Sustainability at [[Louisiana State University]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.che.lsu.edu/news/2012/5/albemarle-lecture-on-sustainability/ |title=Albemarle Lecture |access-date=2015-03-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402091256/http://www.che.lsu.edu/news/2012/5/albemarle-lecture-on-sustainability/ |archive-date=2015-04-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* The State of Green Business Forum<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.greenbiz.com/stateofgreenbusinessforum2011/sf/speakers |title=GreenBiz |access-date=2011-10-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111105184846/http://www.greenbiz.com/stateofgreenbusinessforum2011/sf/speakers |archive-date=2011-11-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* The Distinguished [[Borlaug]] Lecture at [[NC State University]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cnr.ncsu.edu/blogs/news/2010/10/11/anastas-believes-science-technology-offer-%E2%80%98green%E2%80%99-solutions/|title=Borlaug Lecture|access-date=2011-06-25|archive-date=2012-03-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120325191118/http://cnr.ncsu.edu/blogs/news/2010/10/11/anastas-believes-science-technology-offer-%E2%80%98green%E2%80%99-solutions/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
